title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) in sku_delete.php - Arbitrary SKU Deletion
description:
The sku_delete.php endpoint is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attacks. The DELETE operation accepts POST requests without any CSRF token validation, session token verification, Referer/Origin header checking, or authorization validation. An attacker can craft a malicious HTML form on an external website that, when visited by an authenticated user, will automatically submit a DELETE request to the vulnerable endpoint, resulting in arbitrary SKU record deletion without the user's knowledge or consent.

Vulnerable code shows:
- POST requests processed without CSRF token validation
- No session token verification
- No Referer or Origin header checking
- Simple parameter-based deletion mechanism (id parameter)
- No authorization checks to verify user permissions

The attack works because the application relies solely on session cookies for authentication. When an authenticated user visits an attacker-controlled website, their browser automatically includes the session cookies in the cross-site DELETE request, allowing the attacker to perform unauthorized operations.
impact:
An attacker can delete arbitrary SKU records from the database by tricking authenticated users into visiting a malicious webpage. This results in:
- Data loss (SKU records permanently deleted)
- Business disruption (critical product data removed from system)
- Denial of service (legitimate SKU operations disrupted)
- No audit trail of who authorized the deletion
- Potential inventory management chaos and compliance violations
evidence:
POC execution successfully demonstrated the CSRF vulnerability:

1. **Session Establishment**: Created authenticated session via curl with session cookies
2. **Attack Execution**: Sent POST request to sku_delete.php with id parameter, NO CSRF token
3. **Verification**: Confirmed SKU record was deleted - "[+] SKU record appears to have been deleted!"

Output from POC execution shows:
- Response from sku_delete.php accepted the DELETE request without validation
- No error messages indicating missing or invalid CSRF token
- SKU verification step confirms the record no longer exists
- Attack required only authenticated session cookies, no additional validation

The vulnerability was confirmed by examining:
- No CSRF token in POST request handler
- No session verification or authorization checks
- Direct database DELETE operation on user input (id parameter)
- No framework or middleware CSRF protection in place
references: CWE-352: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF), OWASP A01:2021 - Broken Access Control, OWASP Top 10 - CSRF Prevention Cheat Sheet
toolCallDescription: Document CSRF vulnerability in sku_delete.php with confirmed POC showing arbitrary SKU deletion without token validation
